subject: Banking
title: Overend Gurney: Victorian Bank Run
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Overend Gurney: Victorian Bank Run.

hook.text: Overend Gurney was London's biggest discount bank. On May 10, 1866.

buildup.text: The bank had lent recklessly to railway speculators and shipbuilders. When loans went bad, losses exceeded capital.

discovery.text: Depositors rushed to withdraw. The Bank of England refused to bail them out.

twist.text: This crisis established the lender of last resort principle.

climax.text: One bank's failure reshaped central banking. Overend Gurney's collapse created the modern lender of last resort concept.

punchline.text: The Bank of England refused to help. 200 firms failed.

quiz.question: What principle did the Overend Gurney collapse establish?
options: The lender of last resort concept
